regcompR: Distributional Regression with a Verified Registry of Probability Distributions

Source: R/regcompR-package.R
regcompR-package.Rd

A framework for distributional regression in which every parameter of a response distribution can depend on covariates through its own formula (Rigby and Stasinopoulos 2005 doi:10.1111/j.1467-9876.2005.00510.x ). Distributions are held in a machine readable registry that records support, parameter domains, links, moments and their existence conditions, available methods, references and validation status. Count, binary, bounded, categorical, ordinal, real line, positive, unit interval, simplex, circular, extreme value, multivariate and matrix valued laws are provided, each with density or mass, distribution function, quantile, random generation and moments where these exist. Operators build new laws from old ones: inflation, hurdles, truncation, censoring, monotone transformation, discretization, rounding, finite mixtures, convolution, compounding and splicing. Models are fitted by maximum or penalized likelihood with a Laplace approximation for random effects and smooth terms, optionally through 'TMB' (Kristensen et al. 2016 doi:10.18637/jss.v070.i05 ), or by Bayesian inference through generated 'Stan' programs run by 'bayescompR', 'cmdstanr' or 'rstan'. Predictions, quantiles, event probabilities, randomized quantile residuals, proper scoring rules, cross validation, and plots for every distribution and fit are included.
